name: Bournemouth lumbar quantitative fluoroscopy (Breen 2021)
what: weight-bearing and recumbent L2 to S1 flexion and extension cine of 127 subjects at 15 fps, 60 degrees at 6 degrees a second; only per-frame angles are public on OSF
level_truth: lumbar, if corner templates exist as they do for the cervical set
status: the only confirmed lumbar cine; the letter (request 1) went to the Bournemouth team on 2026-10-20 22:44 UTC; Jonny Branney answered on 2026-10-22 and Alex Breen on 2026-10-24: about 1,180 image events in all, 500 to 800 GB, more than the two public databases hold (about 120 cervical flexion and extension, weight-bearing; 280 lumbar flexion and extension, weight-bearing or recumbent; 380 lumbar side flexion; 100 recumbent leg swing; 300 mixed, from smaller studies and clinical referrals), taken on a Siemens Arcadis Avantic C-arm at a fixed source-to-detector distance, 15 fps, 1024 by 1024, 16-bit DICOM, the stored DICOM being the original frames (row 1 of a corner template is the mean of frames 1 and 2), with the corner templates; a data sharing agreement is required and one Wayne State prepares would be quickest; Marcin Budka, chief investigator of MAID, was copied for the licence of the MAID images (OSF z2jby), which Breen was unsure of and which Marcin Budka set on OSF to CC BY-NC 4.0 on 2026-10-25, and which holds only the sequences tracked for all of L2 to S1 on every frame, a sequence that lost one level's track being left out (Breen, 2026-10-24); any DICOM, a27py's lumbar cine included, needs the agreement; frames were averaged in pairs before tracking, so row 1 of a template is the first averaged frame, and MachineAngle came from another device, synchronised by hand to peak excursion and interpolated to the frame rate, which is why its length differs; Breen passed the pixel spacing and image-intensifier distortion question to Fiona Mellor (Exeter), who has not answered; from 2026-10-24 Breen writes from a personal address, since his Bournemouth one ends with his fellowship; Arnold Wong (PolyU) auto-replied on 2026-10-20 naming Ms Chelsia Cheung, to whom the owner forwarded the letter on 2026-10-21 03:57 UTC, with no answer from PolyU; the owner asked Branney on 2026-10-24 03:08 UTC about z2jby's terms and scope, and replied to Breen on 2026-10-24 asking for the agreement and that licence; the copy to Jacqueline Rix (Portsmouth) bounced the same day, the account inactive; nothing from Branney's research department or from Bournemouth since, as of 2026-10-25; waits on the agreement, Wayne State's own sent to Breen, and on Mellor's answer; on 2026-10-26 14:33 UTC Fiona Mellor (Exeter) answered that she will liaise directly with Professor Alan Breen and Dr Alex Breen so that the pixel spacing, the distortion question and the rest come back as one coordinated response, which is now what this waits on; for the owner's tiers of 2026-10-27 every event is a partial spine (cervical C0 to T1, or lumbar L2 to S1) on real fluoroscopy alone, with corner templates a person placed and the tracker followed, so the cine is silver 3 when it comes; tracks and tables carry no pixels, so they place no one in a tier until then
licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 for the MAID images (OSF z2jby), set on OSF by Marcin Budka on 2026-10-25; OSF a27py holds derived tables only
how_to_get: Part of request 1 above: write to the corresponding author of doi:10.3389/fbioe.2021.745837 for the L2-S1 cine behind osf.io/a27py.
